`jmap-types` already exports the `State` newtype (crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs:67):

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct State(String);
```

…and exposes a `State::new_validated` constructor (RFC 8620 §1.2 character set check). Every `since_state` / `since_query_state` request-side field correctly uses `&State` (see e.g. crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/email.rs:72,177). Only the response-side fields drop to raw `String`.

This is a direct parallel of closed bead JMAP-sc1b.48 (4 sites used account_id: String while 52 used Id). Same engineering argument: typed responses make invalid wire values rejectable at deserialize time, eliminate string-typing of values with documented invariants, and align the public API.

Why P2: SemVer-affecting (changes public field types across 7 response structs that are re-exported by 7+ client crates). The fix is mechanical (`String → State`), the wire format is unchanged because `State` is `#[serde(transparent)]`, and it brings the workspace into consistency with the pattern .48 already established for account_id.

Why idiomatic-rust: "Primitive obsession: raw u64 for IDs, String for paths/URIs/names" — workspace AGENTS.md section 1 type-design — "anywhere a newtype would prevent confusion between values of the same primitive type."

Note that jmap-types/State has `AsRef<str>` so .as_ref() callers won't break; constructions via `String::new" or "x.to_string()" become `State::from(...)` or for fallible construction `State::new_validated(...)?`.

Note also: EmailImportResponse was added in commit 72fc913 (5 days ago); the regression was avoidable — the cookie-cutter rule ("jmap-mail-client is canonical for extension-client family") should have forced State, but the canonical itself uses String here, so the new addition propagated the existing inconsistency. Fix in jmap-types first, then propagate per workspace AGENTS.md rule.
title: P2: 5 sites use state: String / old_state: String while jmap-types::State newtype exists
